summary: Explores four NASA items left on the Moon and mars, explaining their significance while emphasizing teamwork, discovery, learning, brain development, and continued space research.
details:
An interactive web platform that brings NASA's retired lunar and Martian rovers back to life by transforming complex open datasets into engaging Japanese Manga storytelling.

Millions of miles away on the Moon and Mars, humanity's greatest robotic pioneers rest in silence after completing historic missions. However, their incredible journey's are often buried inside dense text-heavy scientific archives that can be intimidating for students and the general public Our project bridges the gap between space science and human emotion. Built with clean HTML ad CSS, the website features an intuitive navigation bar allowing users to explore four legendary explores: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV) Opportunity Rover, Phoenix Mars Lander and Ingenuity Helicopter. Each section pairs accurate scientific specification and real NASA archive imagery with custom. dynamic Japanese Manga illustrations generated via meticulous AI prompt engineering This visual approach makes space history accessible, thrilling and memorable.
Use of data & Tools:
We strictly utilized official open datasets engineering and raw imagery from NASA's archives including the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archie (NSSDCA) the Planetary Data System, (PDS) and the JPL Photo-journal. To visualize these datasets, we combined front-end web development (HTML/CSS) with Generative Ai tools to craft custom manga panels that accurately depict key missions milestones. Lastly, were gonna list off why we picked a Apollo mission which was special to us as a team which is Apollo 15 out of Apollo 15,16,17 why we picked Apollo 15 specifically? Apollo 15 was the mission where astronauts tried out the lunar rover for the first time ever on moon, Apollo 15 mission is an extraordinary achievement of the human exploration spending 67 hours on the moon, conducting 19 hours on spacewalks, and collecting hundred's of rock samples
